title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
grouping: Two stacked sub-diagrams, each titled in underlined italic ('Action Chunking', 'Action Chunking + Temporal Ensemble'). Both are grids: timestep numbers 0-7 run along the top as column heads and query times (t=0, t=4 with a vertical ellipsis between; then t=0..t=3) label the rows on the left. No containers beyond the grid itself.
shapes_depth: Each predicted action is a small flat square with a thin dark outline, filled red, orange, yellow or green by its position within a chunk of four. In the upper grid chunks tile end to end; in the lower grid each row shifts one column right, forming a staircase. Light-grey rounded outlines enclose each column of overlapping predictions; the column at timestep 3 has a black outline, and beside it the inline text 'x [0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1] =' leads to one yellow square with a soft glow (the combined action).
proposed_highlight: The one column being combined is ringed in black (others in grey) and its weighted sum is written inline next to it; the result square glows.
lesson: Lay predicted actions on a time x query-step grid of coloured squares (colour = position within the chunk) so overlapping chunks form a staircase, and ring one column to show which predictions are averaged for that timestep.
notes: Method short name ACT (Action Chunking with Transformers) from the paper's caption of Figure 4. Venue RSS from Semantic Scholar (title match, venue_source: semantic-scholar); year 2023 = S2 year and arXiv year. flow 'mixed': time runs left to right, query steps top to bottom.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: bimanual imitation learning, action chunking with temporal ensembling
taxonomy.note: architecture other: the figure shows no network, only a timestep x action-index grid of overlapping predicted action chunks combined by temporal ensembling

core.what: repeated chunk predictions unrolled as rows of a timestep x action-index grid, each query step's chunk shifted one column right so the overlaps form a staircase, with one column ringed to show which predictions are averaged

relations.form: rows t=0..t=3 in the lower panel, each a four-square chunk shifted one column right of the row above, giving a diagonal staircase
two stacked panels sharing the 0-7 index axis: plain 'Action Chunking' above (chunks at t=0 and t=4, no overlap) and 'Action Chunking + Temporal Ensemble' below (a chunk every step)
a bold black rounded outline encloses column 3 across all four rows, and the inline 'x [0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1] =' turns it into one glowing yellow result square at the right of the top row
grey rounded outlines group every other column's stacked predictions, showing the operation repeats on each timestep of the grid

channels.colour: square fill = position within the predicted chunk (red 1st, orange 2nd, yellow 3rd, green 4th), consistent in both panels; the glowing yellow square is the blended action
channels.line: outline weight = selection: black outline = the column being combined now, light grey = other columns' groups
channels.frame: no containers; the two panels are separated only by underlined italic headings

quality.strengths: the core relation is pure geometry - the staircase of shifted chunks shows overlap without any arrows; colour has one meaning (position in chunk) kept identical across both panels, so the eye sees that column 3 mixes four different chunk positions; the plain-chunking panel above sets up the comparison on the same axis
quality.weaknesses: the weight vector equation sits at the end of the top row, a column's width away from the ringed column it applies to; the light grey column outlines are faint and easy to miss

insights.structure: Two stacked sub-panels with underlined italic headings: top 'Action Chunking' shows chunks at t=0 and t=4 laid on a shared action-index axis 0-7; bottom 'Action Chunking + Temporal Ensemble' shows rows t=0..3 each shifted one column right, forming a staircase.
insights.data: Each predicted action is a small coloured square (red, orange, yellow, green by position in the chunk), so the same colour sequence repeats diagonally across rows.
insights.emphasis: A bold black rounded box outlines column 3 across all rows (the actions predicted for one timestep), and an inline equation 'x [0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1] =' turns it into one blended glowing yellow square.
insights.flow: Read top to bottom as time steps and left to right as action index; grey rounded outlines group each column's predictions with no arrows at all.
insights.avoid: The weights equation sits awkwardly on the top row far from the highlighted column, and the light grey column outlines are faint enough to be missed.

arrangement.units: two stacked panels separated only by underlined italic headings; cells are coloured squares in a timestep x index grid, columns grouped by grey rounded outlines
arrangement.inputs_as: column index numbers 0-7 across the top, timestep labels t= down the left
arrangement.shared: the action-index axis is shared by both panels
